chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi, from Abu Ja'far, from Ibn Abi Ghasan, from Humayd ibn Mas'ud, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about throwing the Jamaraat while not in a state of ritual purity. He said: 'The Jamaraat with us are like al-Safa and al-Marwah; they are walls. If you circumambulate between them while not in a state of ritual purity, it will not harm you, but purity is more beloved to me, so do not leave it while you are able to do so.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Then he comes to the farthest Jamrah, which is at al-Aqabah, and he should stand facing it until the end of the door.

key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجِمَارِ: Throwing the pebbles at the Jamaraat

ai.seo_question: Does one need to be in a state of ritual purity (taharah) when throwing the Jamaraat during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that ritual purity is not a strict condition for throwing the Jamaraat, likening them to the walls of the Kaaba where impurity does not invalidate the act, yet he strongly recommends maintaining it as a preferred practice. This ruling highlights the Shia distinction between essential pillars and recommended etiquettes in Hajj rituals. The narration further specifies the precise standing position at the farthest Jamrah (Jamrat al-Aqaba) near the Gate, emphasizing the spatial precision required in this rite.
